inventory.visualPurpose: Exogenous + endogenous lipid transport circuit with seven numbered steps
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: Full-body circuit: small intestine lumen (micelles) → intestinal cell → chylomicron (apo B48) → thoracic duct → subclavian vein → systemic circulation; HDL transfers apo CII/apoE; LPL at capillary → FFA to adipocyte → chylomicron remnant → hepatocyte apoE receptor; hepatocyte (bile canaliculus) → VLDL (apo B100) → LPL → IDL → hepatic lipase → LDL → LDL-receptor endocytosis in peripheral cell; seven numbered callouts with type I/IV/II annotations.

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: Liver (upper left) and small intestine (lower left) both secrete nascent HDL (disc-shaped, apo CII top, apoE bottom) → LCAT on the arrow → mature HDL (sphere with cholesteryl-ester core) → CETP on the arrow → text 'Transfer of cholesteryl esters to VLDL, IDL, LDL'.

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: Seven-row enzyme/function table: CETP, hepatic lipase, hormone-sensitive lipase, LCAT (esterification of 2/3 of plasma cholesterol, HDL maturation), lipoprotein lipase, pancreatic lipase, PCSK9 (degrades LDL receptor; inhibition raises recycling).
